stories.headline: 'Squad' member urges Dems to take advantage of midterm sweep by passing far-left policies
stories.note: A Squad member is already pushing a far-left agenda, giving the GOP a clear overreach message.
body: Rep. Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts, a member of the progressive House 'Squad,' is calling on her party to use its new congressional majorities to pass a sweeping far-left agenda.
In remarks Tuesday she listed Medicare for All, the EACH Act and repeal of the Hyde Amendment, reparations, and defunding and abolishing ICE as the priorities she wants Democrats to deliver.

"When we have the power we have to use it," Pressley said, addressing House colleagues directly. On X a day later she called President Trump "the fascist occupant of the White House" over his moves against DEI.

White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster answered that the president promised to end divisive policies and restore merit, saying DEI under the Biden administration cost Americans through higher costs and inefficiency. Trump can still veto bills from the Democratic Congress in his final two years.
Why it matters: Republicans lost both chambers, but an agenda of reparations and abolishing ICE gives them a clear overreach story to run on heading into 2028.

stories.headline: Inside ICE's high-stakes raids targeting illegal migrants in NYC as chief rips sanctuary laws
stories.note: ICE keeps arresting illegal migrants in NYC while its chief puts sanctuary laws on the spot.
body: Fox News Digital rode along with ICE agents in Brooklyn last Thursday as they made early-morning street arrests of illegal migrants, including a Georgian national charged with sexual abuse.
Ken Genalo, who runs ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations in New York City, said sanctuary rules force agents to hunt suspects on the street instead of picking them up from local jails.
"100% all of this is about politics. It is not about public safety," Genalo said, blaming Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Gov. Kathy Hochul and the City Council.

The ride-along came days after Mamdani released a Spanish-language video advising New Yorkers how to respond to ICE. In August a statewide push called Operation Rotten Apple netted nearly 2,200 arrests.
Why it matters: The story puts a face on the sanctuary-city fight and shows the administration keeps enforcing immigration law even as Democrats gain power.

stories.headline: Trump admin sues Penn State over in-state tuition policy for undocumented migrants
stories.note: The administration is taking a popular fight to court over taxpayer-subsidized tuition for illegal migrants.
body: The Justice Department sued Penn State on Thursday over a policy that lets undocumented students qualify for in-state tuition.
DOJ argues the policy discriminates against U.S. citizens from other states, who can't get the same lower rate, and violates a federal law that bars such benefits unless all citizens get them.

Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate said the university "has ignored that mandate." Penn State's website says undocumented students can qualify after four years at and graduation from a Pennsylvania high school, or a Pennsylvania GED.

It is DOJ's 27th lawsuit against in-state tuition for illegal migrants, and six earlier cases in Texas, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Nebraska, Illinois and Kansas produced orders favoring the federal government.
Why it matters: The administration is pressing an issue most voters see as basic fairness to citizens, with a winning track record in court.

stories.headline: Democrats ‘divorced from voters’ as 5 states back citizen-only voting, bolstering GOP push
stories.note: Even in a Democratic wave year, voters in five states backed a core GOP election-integrity idea.
body: Voters in Kansas, Alaska, Arkansas, South Dakota and West Virginia approved ballot measures making clear that only citizens can vote in state and local elections, each with more than 60% support.

Kansas passed its measure even as Democrats pulled off a Senate upset there, a sign the idea crosses party lines. A 2024 Gallup poll cited in the story found 83% of Americans, including 66% of Democrats, back proof of citizenship for first-time registrants.

Similar measures failed in California, where Proposition 39 lost by about 17 points after the left spent more than $30 million against it, and in Arizona, where the measure covered more than just citizenship.

Former FEC member Hans von Spakovsky said Democrats are "divorced" from their voters, and Jason Snead of the Honest Elections Project called it a 90-10 issue. Democrats have argued the SAVE America Act would disenfranchise eligible voters.
Why it matters: Even in a Democratic wave year, voters endorsed a core GOP election-integrity idea, strengthening the push for proof-of-citizenship rules.

stories.headline: Schumer faces mutiny from newly elected Senate Dems as party prepares to seize power
stories.note: Democrats' new majority is already fighting over its own leader.
body: Chuck Schumer is favored to stay on as Senate Democratic leader in the new 54-seat majority, but several incoming senators say they don't want him.
Kansas Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton, who unseated Roger Marshall, called Schumer "a liability for Democrats" in his state and said the party needs younger leadership.

Maine's Troy Jackson said he told Schumer he would back someone else, and Illinois' Juliana Stratton, Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed and Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan are also not fully on board. Some progressives have floated Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who is weighing a 2028 run.
Schumer insists he'll be re-elected leader, telling reporters, "The issue is not me." He needs only a simple majority of his caucus.
Why it matters: Before taking the gavel, the new Democratic majority is already split over leadership and direction.

stories.headline: DOJ launches criminal probe into Supreme Court leak that exposed ruling overturning Roe v Wade
stories.note: The DOJ is finally chasing the Dobbs leaker, a long-standing conservative demand.
body: The Justice Department is running a criminal investigation into the 2022 leak of the draft Supreme Court opinion that overturned Roe v. Wade, sources told Fox News.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro's office in Washington is leading the probe, which has been underway for at least a year and has issued grand jury subpoenas. DOJ declined to comment.
The court's own investigation, led by Marshal Gail Curley, interviewed nearly 100 employees and concluded in January 2023 that it couldn't identify the leaker.
Justice Samuel Alito recently told Fox's Shannon Bream he has an opinion on who did it but not enough evidence, and said the leak made the majority "targets for assassination."
Why it matters: Conservatives have long demanded accountability for a leak that endangered the justices, and a real criminal probe may finally deliver it.

stories.headline: Hegseth expands National Guard operations in DC, authorizes police patrol cars, Humvees and boats
stories.note: Hegseth doubles down on the DC crime crackdown despite the Dem takeover of Congress.
body: War Secretary Pete Hegseth signed an Oct. 29 memo letting National Guard troops in Washington, D.C., use up to 60 marked patrol cars, Humvees and tactical vehicles, Guard boats and up to 20 light towers and generators.
About 3,000 Guard troops are deployed in the capital under President Trump's crime crackdown, which a War Department official called the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful mission.

D.C. Councilmember Brooke Pinto held a hearing Thursday pushing back, calling the presence unnecessary and unlawful, and urged newly elected Democratic governors in five states to pull their 628 troops.
Pinto also wants congressional Democrats to step up oversight of federal law enforcement in January, including badges and body cameras.
Why it matters: The administration is doubling down on its law-and-order push in the capital despite the Democratic takeover of Congress.
